title: Daryl Bem's backward causality study and failed replications

tellings.quote: the replication crisis started in 2010 with Daryl Beam's research on the backward causality, that's how it began.

plain: The psychologist Daryl Bem of Cornell University published research in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, appearing around 2010 and 2011, that claimed to show backward causality: people seeming to respond to events before those events happened. According to the well-known skeptic Michael Shermer, other researchers then tried to repeat the experiments and could not get the same results, and he says this is how psychology's "replication crisis" began, the wider discovery that many published findings do not hold up. Shermer gives this from his own knowledge of the field, mentioning other researchers such as Ray Hyman, Richard Wiseman and Stuart Ritchie.
